subject: Culture
title: Sacred vs Profane
description: A quick win: understand Sacred vs Profane.

hook.text: Step over the threshold of a Shinto shrine and you enter a different reality. A torii gate marks the boundary.

buildup.text: Émile Durkheim argued all cultures divide the world into sacred and profane—set apart and ordinary.

discovery.text: Sacred spaces require rituals to enter: removing shoes, washing hands, covering heads, or bowing.

twist.text: These thresholds aren't decorative. They trigger a psychological shift that primes the brain for reverence.

climax.text: Even secular spaces use this trick. Courtrooms have railings, stages have curtains—boundaries create gravity.

punchline.text: A boundary turns any space into a stage for meaning.

quiz.question: Who proposed the sacred-profane divide as a universal cultural feature?
